status: Pre-run pilot specification; source examples are familiar and the analyst has inspected the code and some dictionary rows. This is an automated answer-withholding test, not a human-blinded decipherment or a preregistered study.

primary_cases.source: Parpola 2010, A Dravidian solution, printed p.13; Woods 2010/2015, Visible Language, phonetization discussion
Parpola 2008, Is the Indus script indeed not a writing system?, printed p.127; ORACC gi[turn]
Woods 2010/2015, Visible Language, phonetization discussion: sar garden → write

secondary_cases.source: Parpola 2010, printed p.13; shares TI with TI_life, not an independent fourth sign

rules.engine: Unmodified Key2A CleanCognateLex, normalizers, stem rule and eval_edges_vectorized; build lexica with the upstream builders in an isolated external cache.
rules.primary: phon_exact with original distinct-cluster restriction; raw primary-case hit count; tied languages remain tied
sensitivities: allow distinct entries despite shared cluster; no pronunciation retuning
rules.controls: All six permutations of the three primary B domains; two full derangements form the pure foil condition. These are foil hit rates, not independently established false historical readings. No 0.0002 p-values from replicating six arrangements.
rules.truth: Stored separately in truth.json; run.py does not read it. score.py reads truth only after search results exist.
rules.limits: Only three independent sign groups. Fixed broad English/German matching is a pilot; source lexica are unequal. No definitive Dravidian/non-Dravidian verdict follows from this pilot.
